Student Performance Data Analysis and Visualization

Pandas | Matplotlib | Seaborn

This notebook applies the data-analysis and visualization operations from the class material to the UCI Student Performance (student-mat.csv) dataset.

Dataset: Student performance in Mathematics
Rows: 395
Columns: 33

Keep student-mat.csv in the same folder as this notebook.

In [1]:
# Import required libraries
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

%matplotlib inline

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Grade improvement from G1 to G3

In [15]:
# Create a performance category using apply() and lambda
def performance_category(grade):
    if grade >= 15:
        return "Excellent"
    elif grade >= 10:
        return "Good"
    else:
        return "Needs Improvement"

df["Performance_Category"] = df["G3"].apply(performance_category)

df[["G3", "Performance_Category"]].head(10)
Out[15]:

3 15 Excellent
4 10 Good
5 15 Excellent

8 19 Excellent
9 15 Excellent

In [18]:
# Example of filling missing numerical values
# (This does not change the original data because the result is stored separately.)
df_filled = df.copy()
df_filled["G3"] = df_filled["G3"].fillna(df_filled["G3"].mean())

df_filled["G3"].isnull().sum()
Out[18]:
np.int64(0)
In [19]:
# Forward fill and backward fill examples
df_ffill = df.copy()
df_ffill = df_ffill.ffill()

df_bfill = df.copy()
df_bfill = df_bfill.bfill()

print("Forward-fill completed:", df_ffill.isnull().sum().sum(), "missing values remain")
print("Backward-fill completed:", df_bfill.isnull().sum().sum(), "missing values remain")
Out[19]:
Forward-fill completed: 0 missing values remain
Backward-fill completed: 0 missing values remain
In [20]:
# Drop rows containing missing values

print("Original rows:", len(df))
print("Rows after dropna():", len(df_dropna))

Original rows: 395
Rows after dropna(): 395

Matplotlib Visualizations

10. Line Plot — Absences vs Final Grade

In [30]:
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
sorted_df = df.sort_values("absences")
plt.plot(sorted_df["absences"], sorted_df["G3"], marker="o", linestyle="-", alpha=0.5)
plt.xlabel("Absences")
plt.ylabel("Final Grade (G3)")
plt.title("Absences vs Final Grade")
plt.show()
Out[30]:

11. Bar Chart — Average Final Grade by Gender

In [31]:
avg_gender_grade = df.groupby("sex")["G3"].mean()

plt.figure(figsize=(7, 5))
plt.bar(avg_gender_grade.index, avg_gender_grade.values)
plt.xlabel("Gender")
plt.ylabel("Average Final Grade")
plt.title("Average Final Grade by Gender")
plt.show()
Out[31]:

12. Grouped Bar Chart — Average Grades by Study Time and Gender

In [32]:
grouped = df.groupby(["studytime", "sex"])["G3"].mean().unstack()

ax = grouped.plot(kind="bar", figsize=(9, 5))
ax.set_xlabel("Study Time")
ax.set_ylabel("Average Final Grade")
ax.set_title("Average Final Grade by Study Time and Gender")
plt.xticks(rotation=0)
plt.show()
Out[32]:

28. Correlation Heatmap

    "age", "studytime", "failures", "absences", "G1", "G2", "G3"

Conclusion

The Student Performance dataset was analyzed using Pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn.

The notebook demonstrates: - Data loading and inspection - Selection and filtering - Creating calculated columns - Missing-value checking and cleaning - Grouping and aggregation - Sorting - Pivot tables - Data export - Line, bar, grouped bar, scatter, histogram, pie and box plots - Subplots - Seaborn scatter, line, bar, count, histogram, violin and box plots - Pair plot and correlation heatmap

These operations follow the same major concepts demonstrated in the supplied class material, adapted to the Student Performance dataset.
